subject: Information Theory
title: Image Compression
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Image Compression.

hook.text: A raw photo from your phone is 30 MB. JPEG shrinks it to 3 MB. You can't tell the difference.

buildup.text: JPEG uses the discrete cosine transform to convert pixel blocks into frequency components.

discovery.text: The eye is less sensitive to high-frequency detail. JPEG discards those components first, saving the most space.

twist.text: Push compression too far and blocky artifacts appear—the hallmark of over-compressed JPEG images.

climax.text: Information theory defines the minimum: you can't compress below the image's entropy without losing quality.

punchline.text: Remove what eyes can't see. Keep what matters.

quiz.question: How does JPEG achieve compression?
options: By discarding high-frequency detail the eye can't see
By converting to black and white
